maria: :rotating_light: quick recap — ~02:12 UTC we started seeing intermittent egress failures from west-coast public subnets. Observed ~30% GPU allocate failures for small batch jobs, autoscaler spun extra nodes, and we triggered traffic shifts to AMS and SFO. Opening thread to collect concrete runbook updates and action items.
kevin: timeline + root cause? was it healthchecks flipping or a provider-level egress issue?
srebot: ALERT: west-coast-egress — packet_loss > 5% for 8m; alloc_fail_rate spike 0.31 at 04:13Z. Linked logs: https://logs.internal/reports/1834567890
ashley: Mitigation we applied: throttled outbound egress rules for a subset of tenants to reduce blast radius, then started the playbook traffic-shift to AMS. Latency rose but allocations succeeded.
diego: Noticed autoscaler doubled nodes which caused a cost surge and increased cold-starts for KV cache. We should add a warm-pool/reserve recommendation to avoid reallocation thrash.
maria: Proposed runbook changes (sketch):
- Add a preflight egress check that runs automatically before large rotations/deploys and as a manual step in the playbook.
- Add a typed "fast-traffic-shift" CLI with validation (route tables, KV compatibility, cache flush) and a canary window.
- Add a cost-gating step to autoscaler bursts (notify + optional hold if cost delta > threshold).
kevin: +1 to all. Can you draft the CLI usage we want to include so infra-scripts can implement it?
diego: Suggested CLI prototype: 
```
redwood infra traffic-shift --from=west-coast --to=ams --weight=0.6 --canary=5m --dry-run
```
This should run validations: route table sanity, probe egress to public endpoints, and do a KV-prefix compatibility check before applying.
ashley: Also add explicit netlink/flap detection commands in the runbook so on-call can triage quickly: 
```
kubectl -n infra get events --field-selector reason=NetworkUnreachable
ip -s link show dev eth0 | grep -E "dropped|errors"
```
maria: Concrete action items (owner — due):
1) Diego — add warm-pool sizing table + recommendation to runbook, include example costs for N=1/2/3 GPUs (due 48h).
2) Ashley — add netlink/flap detection + remediation steps (netpol rollback, route reattach) and a short checklist (due 24h).
3) Kevin — implement the traffic-shift CLI in infra-scripts repo + unit tests + dry-run mode (due 72h).
4) Maria — update the playbook document, link the CLI, and coordinate a dry-run next week (due 7d).
srebot: NOTE: incident ticket #INC-20260317 created and linked to this thread.
ops-runbooks-bot: Runbook drafted: /runbooks/west-coast-egress (draft) — please review :clipboard: https://runbooks.internal/west-coast-egress/draft
kevin: Quick question — do we want a budget/cost alert when autoscaler > X for Y minutes? We saw a ~27% cost bump during the surge.
diego: Yes. Propose alert: autoscaler.scale_count_delta > 2 within 10m -> cost-notify + manual hold option. Add sample alert rule in runbook snippet.
maria: Also add a pre-shift cache safety step: flush or set graceful-deny on KV prefixes to avoid token duplication and large cold-cache penalties.
ashley: One-line cache snippet to put in the playbook: 
```
cachectl flush-prefix --prefix=kv/prefix-<deployment> --grace=30s
```
diego: Scheduling: let's run a dry-run traffic shift + tabletop next Tue 16:00 UTC. Will coordinate calendar invite.
maria: :thumbsup: please ping this thread after PRs are opened. We'll close the loop after the dry-run and a follow-up postmortem doc. Thanks team.
